::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jany 17th [1873?]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Pennsylvania
:::

Dear [Mrs White](people/person_1494.qmd)
I cannot remember Miss [Evelyn Gee](people/person_553.qmd)’s present address, so would you be so kind as to forward this note to her containing a request from some one in Sloane Street to print her [Eagle Story](other_books/otherbook_820.qmd), which certainly has been a great favourite[^1]

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Another example of this paper dates from July 1882.
[^2]: CMY’s bank account records the payment of £5 to Miss E. Gee on 10 April 1873, the only one to a person of this name.  A story ‘What the Church Eagle Said’ appeared in *MP* (?Christmas 1872) 4.  Evelyn Gee (b. Herts. 1843/4), daughter of the Rev. Richard Gee, Vicar of Abbots Langley and later of Windsor, who married 1880 Richard Rivington Holmes, librarian at Windsor Castle, seems a plausible candidate.  He has an entry in ODNB, which states that she survived him.  No separate publication of the story has been traced.
